title: fix: Gateway repeatedly rebuilds directory watches above 256 agents
body:
Fixes #171700
Related: #171778

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes repeated filesystem preparation that occupies the Gateway main thread when a configured fleet exceeds 256 agent directories.

## User Impact

Large registered fleets reuse prepared directories across repeated walks, leaving the Gateway more time to serve requests. Native invalidation, cleanup, and the existing 30-second authority/degraded and five-minute healthy recovery bounds remain intact. No configuration, protocol, schema, dependency, or migration changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

The prepared-path capacity now grows with registered directories while keeping extra aliases bounded. The directory-observation owner examines only the changed directory when advancing its timer; closing a subscription does not scan the observation set. Recovery still scans current entries when the timer fires. Removing the earliest subscriber can leave one harmless early recovery pass.

Per-agent startup guards prepare only the selected agent's native directory. All configured session-store claims still enter the physical collision resolver before selecting an owner, preserving fixed, shared, and ACP-only stores.

Original fix by @Leon-SK668; maintainer cleanup simplifies the timer using @chelsealong's approach from #171778 and expands deterministic work-count regressions. The sibling's production repair is covered here; it remains open for the coordinator to handle.

## Evidence

Source and history confirm both defects on main `482631a7d880`: fixed 256-path FIFO eviction and a full observation scan/timer replacement per observe or final close. The original behavior came from `3ac0c058fe16` and `1798288f3522`.

PR CI is the test gate per maintainer policy. It covers the changed agent/infra/session-target regression files, their relevant Gateway/startup siblings, typechecks, lint, and other selected CI gates. Regressions:

- `reuses observations across walks of %i registered agents` covers 64, 256, and 810 agents, unchanged ownership, zero warm-walk realpaths/new watches/closed watches.
- `bounds scheduling work while 810 directories subscribe and close` limits clock-read work per addition, requires no scheduling clock reads on close, retains one timer, delivers the surviving callback, and removes the final timer.
- `selects one database owner without changing %s store ownership` covers default/template/fixed/shared layouts, ACP-only owners, and missing owners with independent expected paths.

Changed-file `oxfmt`, static `oxlint`, and `git diff --check` passed. The nested checkout uses the parent's installed tools; its wrapper could not resolve dependencies, and the parent's install lacks the unrelated Solid lint plugin. Static lint used the same root rules and core tsconfig with only the nonmatching `ui/**/*.tsx` override omitted. All applicable core/test rules remained enabled. No dependencies were installed or changed.

Live Gateway proof, leases, local tests/typechecks, benchmarks, and production-reverted negative controls were intentionally skipped per maintainer policy. The previous contributor reported zero watch recreation at 257/810 agents and a successful 257-agent Gateway run at `7e3e2484514e7fe2da560cae6a31b422935484ee`; those historical reports do not prove this revised head. The full 810-agent production profile and previously reported fresh-directory first-admission heap failure remain outside the measured claim.

Test cost: two additional parameter cases over the original PR's tests; no sleeps or real timer waits added. CI timings are recorded below; no local runtime measurement was performed.

ClawSweeper's full reviews of both candidates had no actionable code findings, and there were no human findings. Its latest review covers this exact head (`99ef70574233302e87c99a65a19c19a9222eb8b3`) and again reports no code findings. The remaining live Gateway, fresh-install/stable-upgrade, and negative-control requests are proof-only asks superseded by the explicit maintainer policy: **PR CI is the proof**. No claim of revised-head live verification is made.

Deferred-fact audit: recovery reads the live directory map and verifies entry identity before filesystem reattachment/notification; paths are immutable entry identities, source and listeners are read from the entry, and current clocks and subscriber intervals govern recovery. The timer captures no config, agent/session binding, or authority. Startup retains its current-config, admission, abort, and lifetime guards; selection only narrows native preparation.

Production LOC: **+37/-15, net +22** (four files), down from the original net +37. Tests: **+135/-2, net +133** (three files); docs: **+0/-0**. Remaining production growth carries the dynamic capacity, one armed deadline, and requested-owner selection. Removing the alias bound or physical-collision checks solely to reach nonpositive LOC would weaken existing contracts.

Deslop removed the extra stored deadline object, deadline arrays/maps, and duplicated scheduling state while keeping the existing owners and bounds. Precommit Codex autoreview was scoped-clean through P2; committed-branch review and exact-head CI results are recorded below.

Committed-branch Codex autoreview: **scoped-clean through P2**, no accepted/actionable findings (reviewed `f9f4a6302633`). Main `3db9d0dc1687` was merged normally; the seven reviewed files are byte-identical after the merge. Final candidate: `99ef70574233302e87c99a65a19c19a9222eb8b3`. Exact-head [CI run 38584282937](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/38584282937) **passed**, including the aggregate `openclaw/ci-gate`, all selected tests, production/test typechecks, lint, build, and guards. No failures, retries, or inherited-failure exceptions were needed.

Exact-head CI log readback:

| Changed test file | Passed cases | Vitest file-lane duration |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| `src/agents/agent-dir-registry.test.ts` | 11 | 3.90 s |
| `src/infra/owned-directory-observation.test.ts` | 8 | 1.18 s |
| `src/config/sessions/targets.selection.test.ts` | 7 | 3.29 s |

The 810-agent registry case passed in 231 ms; the 810-directory scheduling case passed in 97 ms. These are CI test durations, not Gateway latency benchmarks. The unchanged worker-exclusion regression also passed (one case, 1.47 s file lane), and Gateway startup/preparation siblings passed in the selected hosted lane. Final live check readback: **71 passing checks, 56 intentionally skipped, none pending or failed**.
